solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/symmetric-tree/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

101. Symmetric Tree

Given the root of a binary tree, check whether it is a mirror of itself (i.e., symmetric around its center).

Example 1:

Input: root = [1,2,2,3,4,4,3]
Output: true

Example 2:

Input: root = [1,2,2,null,3,null,3]
Output: false

Constraints:

    The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 1000].
    -100 <= Node.val <= 100

Follow up: Could you solve it both recursively and iteratively?
"""


class Solution:
    def isSymmetric(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> bool:
        if not root:
            return True

        def is_mirror(t1: Optional[TreeNode], t2: Optional[TreeNode]) -> bool:
            if not t1 and not t2:
                return True
            if not t1 or not t2:
                return False
            return (
                t1.val == t2.val
                and is_mirror(t1.left, t2.right)
                and is_mirror(t1.right, t2.left)
            )

        return is_mirror(root.left, root.right)


sol = Solution()

print(sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 3])))  # True

assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 3])) is True
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, 2, 2, None, 3, None, 3])) is False

assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([])) == True
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1])) == True
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, 1, 1, 1, None, None, 1])) == True
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, 2, 2, 3, None, None, 3])) == True
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, -2, -2, -3, -4, -4, -3])) == True
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, 2, 2, 2, None, 2])) == False
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1] * 1000)) == False
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([i for i in range(1, 1001)])) == False
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([0] * 7)) == True
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, 2, 2, None, None, None, None])) == True
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3])) == True
assert sol.isSymmetric(build_tree([1, -1, -1, -2, -3, -3, -2])) == True
